summary:
The record mostly holds. I could not refute any of its runtime claims. Weight sizes, the config and the KV arithmetic (36,864 B/token BF16) all re-verified exactly. The vLLM "does not fit" verdict is correct (-47.3 GiB). The v0.33.0 registry, the parser names and the sm_120 Marlin demotion for MXFP4 are confirmed at the tag.

Corrections:
(1) I parsed the real GGUF header with a range read. Experts total 56.88 GiB (1.58 GiB per layer) and non-expert tensors 2.14 GiB, because attention is Q8_0 in this GGUF, not BF16. With --n-cpu-moe 32 that puts about 50.6 GiB in RAM. The conclusions do not change.
(2) The guide's 16 GB recipe is 32k context with -ub 4096. The 64k variant is the record's own extrapolation.
(3) The record missed open llama.cpp issue #30781: the gpt-oss template returns HTTP 500 for any tool whose array parameter has no 'items'. The bug is still in the b12418 template and in the template embedded in the ggml-org GGUF. Workaround: --chat-template-file with "'items' in param_spec".
(4) llama.cpp's --fit assumes unlimited host RAM, so it will not prevent the RAM shortfall.

Realistic best configuration: llama.cpp server-cuda13, ggml-org MXFP4 GGUF, -c 65536, --n-cpu-moe 31 or 32, q8_0 KV optional, and a patched template if OpenCode or MCP tool schemas include arrays without items. It only works with about 52 GiB of free RAM, i.e. most desktop apps closed, and gives an estimated 15-20 t/s.

Gaps:
- No measured speed on this laptop.
- Not checked whether OpenCode v2.3.0's built-in tool schemas trigger #30781.
- Not checked whether llama.cpp CPU repack buffers for MXFP4 bypass mmap and raise anonymous RAM use.

Scratch files: $SCRATCH/v120/ and $SCRATCH/parse_gguf.py
